summary: Recommendation: spend almost nothing. Build the historical spine on the Premier League's own Pulselive API - free, unauthenticated, no robots.txt, Opta-keyed via altIds, and it solves P1 (starting XI + bench + substitution minutes + referee, ONE request per fixture) back to at least 2010/11 with 35 seasons listed. It also gives per-player-per-SEASON tackles/interceptions/clearances/blocks/recoveries back to 2006/07 free. P5 also turned out free: football-data.co.uk is reachable again and ships opening AND closing odds plus O/U 2.5 and Asian handicap per match back to 1993/94 as bulk CSV. The only thing worth buying is per-match defensive actions: API-Football Pro for ONE month (~$19, third-party-reported price, vendor page is Cloudflare-403) gives tackles/blocks/interceptions per player per fixture from season 2016, 3800 calls fits one day of quota, then cancel. Runner-up TheStatsAPI $50/mo (verified pricing page) - only affordable source with per-player-per-match xG/npxG/xA plus clearances and 10 years, but unknown vendor, no Opta ids, no blocks, no recoveries. NOT recommended: Sportmonks (P2 unverifiable without signup, no Opta lineage, history behind a one-time add-on), all enterprise vendors (quote-only, they sell the Opta data the PL API gives us free). Answer to the three questions: (1) no single affordable provider covers P1+P2 with 5+ seasons; (2) P2 is cheap-and-partial at best - recoveries per player per match are unobtainable from every affordable source, which is exactly why DC is a real moat; (3) cheapest config that unblocks P1+P2 is roughly $19 one-off on top of four free sources. footballdata.io OpenAPI spec carries x-plan annotations per endpoint. EVERY player endpoint is x-plan:free (/players, /players/{id}, /players/{id}/stats, /teams/{id}/players). Section 11 permits building analysis tools and internal systems but forbids exposing raw data as a database or downloadable dataset. Sections 16 and 22 disclaim accuracy and explicitly attribute data to third-party providers - they are an aggregator, not a collector.

FPLProvider.fetch_batch() exists because bootstrap-static/ answers 6 of the 7 capabilities this slice serves in ONE HTTP call. detail: CANONICAL_SCHEMAS[MANAGER_PICKS_SELECTION_GAMEWEEK].entity_key was (entry_id, element) -- missing 'event' (gameweek). That was a latent bug: nothing exercised it because no production caller used as_of()/latest() with an entity_key before this story. Had it shipped unfixed, as_of('picks', t) would have state-collapsed a manager's picks across DIFFERENT gameweeks into one row for the same (entry,element) pair, silently discarding all but the latest gameweek's picks -- exactly the EO/captaincy data blueprint SS3.4 says has no archive and no recovery path. Fixed to (entry_id, event, element).

Caller audit: zero production callers of as_of()/latest() existed anywhere in src/ or scripts/ before this story -- both ingest scripts only call store.write(); providers/fpl.py imports only content_hash from store.py. schemas.py: added DATASET_ENTITY_KEYS (dataset-name -> entity_key tuple, () for singleton), derived from CANONICAL_SCHEMAS so there is one declared source of truth, not two. Fixed picks entity_key to include 'event'.

Added observations(dataset, until=t): the raw stream, explicit opt-in, works for any dataset incl. undeclared ones since there is no state to collapse to. latest() simplified to as_of(dataset, now). BitemporalStore.as_of() is unsafe on vaastav_player_gameweek_stats: its declared entity_key is (season, round, element), but real double/triple gameweeks put 2-3 rows under that exact same key (verified live: 2020-21 GW35, Bruno Fernandes, 3 fixture rows, same batch_id, different opponent/kickoff/points -- a Covid-rearrangement triple gameweek). as_of() QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER()=1 would silently keep only 1 of the 2-3 fixtures per entity, undercounting any double/triple-GW player. This is the same class of silent-corruption bug blueprint section 3.2 already fixed once for as_of() returning duplicated observations -- this is the mirror-image failure (as_of() dropping legitimate non-duplicate rows that happen to share an entity key). The backtest harness therefore uses observations() exclusively for this dataset, never as_of(), and groups by (season, round, element) explicitly, summing across fixtures within a round rather than assuming one row. This should be called out in provider-framework.md / schemas.py PLAYER_GAMEWEEK_STATS_GAMEWEEK docstring so a future caller does not reach for as_of() on this dataset by habit.
